primitives.name: Closed Subgroup Invariance
primitives.verbatim_quote: If μ is any Baire measure in a locally compact topological group X, and if Y is the set of all those elements y for which μ(yE) = μ(E) for all Baire sets E, then Y is a closed subgroup of X.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'μ': 'Baire measure on topological group X', 'Y': 'subset of X, elements satisfying μ(yE) = μ(E)', 'E': 'Baire set in X'}
primitives.assumptions: X is a locally compact topological group, μ is a Baire measure, E is a Baire set.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When μ fails to be regular or E is not Baire measurable.

layer2.mapping: The set Y represents the kernel of measure-preserving automorphisms within X, enabling GSI to define invariant likelihoods.
layer2.telemetry: Measure equality μ(yE) = μ(E) across all Baire sets E.

primitives.name: Locally Bounded Group Embedding
primitives.verbatim_quote: If, however, we make use of the fact that every locally bounded group may be viewed as a dense subgroup of a locally compact group, then we may reformulate our results in a somewhat more useful way.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'G': 'locally bounded group', 'H': 'locally compact group containing G as dense subgroup'}
primitives.assumptions: G is locally bounded, H is locally compact, G ⊆ H densely.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When embedding fails due to non-Hausdorff or non-second-countable structure.

layer2.mapping: Embedding allows GSE to extend local boundedness into global compactness for state transition modeling.
layer2.telemetry: Density of G in H and preservation of topological properties.

primitives.name: Measure Preservation Closure
primitives.verbatim_quote: Applying this conclusion to yo-1 and y0C in place of yo and C we obtain the reverse inequality, and hence the identity, μ(C) = μ(yoC) for all C.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'yo': 'element of Y, fixed point in subgroup', 'C': 'compact Baire set', 'μ': 'regular Baire measure'}
primitives.assumptions: μ is regular, C is compact Baire set, Y is defined by μ-invariance.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure of regularity or compactness of C.

layer2.mapping: Closure of Y ensures μ-invariance holds globally, enabling GSI to model stable probabilistic dynamics.
layer2.telemetry: Equality μ(C) = μ(yoC) for all compact Baire sets C.

The derivation begins with the foundational notion of a Baire measure μ on a locally compact topological group X. For any subset Y ⊆ X, the condition μ(yE) = μ(E) for all Baire sets E defines a subgroup structure. The proof proceeds by showing that Y is closed under group operations and inverses, establishing it as a closed subgroup. This closure property hinges on the regularity of μ and the compactness of Baire sets. The key insight is that measure invariance under left translation implies a structural constraint on the group's topology. When extended to locally bounded groups, these results can be embedded into larger compact groups, allowing for richer topological and measure-theoretic analysis. The failure mode occurs when μ lacks regularity or when E is not Baire measurable, breaking the equivalence μ(yE) = μ(E). These primitives form the basis for constructing conformal mappings in GSI and for defining state transitions in GSE where topological invariance is preserved.
